title.en: Draw the block diagram of a regulated d.c. power supply

say.en: When the mains dips from 230 volts to 200 volts, or you plug in a bigger load, a plain filtered supply sags. A regulated supply holds its output steady. In this lesson: Draw the block diagram of a regulated d.c. power supply.
Define line and load regulation.
Use three-terminal IC regulators (78xx, 79xx).

title.en: Blocks of a regulated power supply

body.en: A regulated d.c. *power supply* has four blocks: a step-down transformer (230 V a.c. to a lower a.c. voltage, also isolating the circuit from the mains), a rectifier (a.c. to pulsating d.c.), a filter (removes most of the ripple) and a voltage regulator (keeps the output constant against changes in the input voltage and the load current). A Zener diode with a series resistor is the simplest regulator.

points.en: Unregulated *supply*: output changes with mains and load

narration.en: A regulated supply has four blocks: transformer, rectifier, filter and regulator. The regulator keeps the output steady when the mains or the load changes.

title.en: Blocks of a regulated d.c. power supply

say.en: A regulated supply has four blocks. The transformer steps 230 volts down to a few volts.
The rectifier makes it one-way, and the filter smooths the pulses into d.c. with a little ripple.
The regulator holds the output steady even when the mains voltage or the load changes.
A three-terminal IC like the 7805 is the regulator in most supplies: input, ground and a steady plus five volts out.
Regulation tells how much the output drops on load. Smaller is better; an ideal supply has zero percent.

body.en: Load regulation measures how much the output falls from no load to full load: $\%\,\text{Reg} = (V_{NL} - V_{FL})/V_{FL} \times 100$; an ideal supply has 0 %. Line regulation measures the change in output for a change in input voltage. Three-terminal *IC regulators* make regulation easy: the 78xx series gives fixed positive outputs (7805 → +5 V, 7812 → +12 V), the 79xx series fixed negative outputs, and the LM317 an adjustable output. The input must be at least about 2 V above the output (the dropout voltage).

narration.en: Percentage regulation is V no-load minus V full-load, over V full-load, times one hundred. IC regulators such as the 7805 give a fixed, steady output.
narration.kn: ಶೇಕಡಾ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ = (V_NL − V_FL)/V_FL × 100. 7805 ನಂತಹ IC ನಿಯಂತ್ರಕಗಳು ಸ್ಥಿರ ಔಟ್‌ಪುಟ್ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ.

problem.en: A power supply gives 12.6 V on no load and 12.0 V when it delivers its full-load current of 1 A. Find the percentage regulation and its output resistance.

steps.en: The drop of 0.6 V at 1 A means an output resistance R_o = 0.6/1 = 0.6 Ω.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A power supply gives 12.6 V on no load and 12.0 V when it delivers its full-load current of 1 A. Find the percentage regulation and its output resistance.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A power supply gives 12.6 volts on no load and 12.0 volts when it delivers its full-load current of 1 A. Find the percentage regulation and its output resistance.
% Reg equals 12.6 minus 12.0/12.0 times 100 equals 0.6 over 12 times 100 equals 5 percent.
The drop of 0.6 volts at 1 A means an output resistance R o equals 0.6 over 1 equals 0.6 ohms.
So the answer is 5 percent; R o equals 0.6 ohms.

problem.en: A 7805 regulator needs at least 2 V more at its input than its output. What is the lowest d.c. input it can work from, and what does it give?

steps.en: Minimum input ≈ 5 + 2 = 7 V d.c. (after the filter, including the bottom of the ripple).

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A 7805 regulator needs at least 2 V more at its input than its output. What is the lowest d.c. input it can work from, and what does it give?

say.en: Let us solve this together. A 7805 regulator needs at least 2 volts more at its input than its output. What is the lowest d.c. input it can work from, and what does it give?
Output of 7805 = plus 5 volts.
Minimum input is approximately 5 plus 2 equals 7 volts d.c. (after the filter, including the bottom of the ripple).
So the answer is About 7 volts in; plus 5 volts out.
